priority: background; does not block Vehicle C, figure machinery, or PPO work

task1.name: leave-one-out refit

prediction.working_hypothesis: Turning-circle-only coverage under-constrains the fast rudder transient response exercised by zig-zags.
prediction.prospective_prediction: Held-out zig-zag trajectories will have larger primary held-out error than held-out turning-circle trajectories because the two turning circles are relatively redundant while zig-zags exercise distinct transient regimes.
prediction.support_rule: Supported only if every held-out zig-zag primary error is greater than both held-out turning-circle primary errors (min zig-zag error > max turning-circle error).
prediction.contradiction_rule: If the strict separation rule is not met, this leave-one-out result does not support the coverage-gap hypothesis and Task 3 must not proceed on that assumption without review.
prediction.aggregation_guard: All six folds must be reported individually. Group extrema are used only to evaluate the precommitted ordering prediction; no six-case average is a verdict.

result.model_scope: KVLCC2 MARIN L7 model-scale diagnostic; no Vehicle B USV coefficient validation

prediction_comparison.expected_ordering: error less than all four zig-zag folds
error less than all four zig-zag folds
error greater than both turning-circle folds
error greater than both turning-circle folds
error greater than both turning-circle folds
error greater than both turning-circle folds

prediction_assessment.rule: Supported only if every held-out zig-zag primary error is greater than both held-out turning-circle primary errors (min zig-zag error > max turning-circle error).
prediction_assessment.statement: The per-fold errors do not strictly separate by maneuver type; Task 1 does not support the coverage-gap hypothesis.

result.aggregation_guard: All six folds must be reported individually. Group extrema are used only to evaluate the precommitted ordering prediction; no six-case average is a verdict.
result.immutability: This diagnostic does not alter the original preregistered protocol, original fit, or scoped-negative-result artifact.

task1.conclusion: The strict predicted separation is false: maximum turning-circle held-out normalized MSE (1.923593) exceeds minimum zig-zag held-out normalized MSE (0.778946). The coverage-gap hypothesis is not supported by Task 1.

task2.name: bound sensitivity

predictions.tightly_bounded_prediction: If the original constraints were merely too tight, at least one formerly pinned coefficient should converge away from the relaxed bounds and held-out zig-zag error should improve substantially.
predictions.underdetermined_prediction: If turning-circle data do not constrain these terms, a formerly pinned coefficient will run to a relaxed bound or the fit will remain unstable/non-improving.
predictions.substantial_improvement_rule: At least 20% reduction from the original fit in both the median held-out zig-zag heading RMSE and median held-out zig-zag yaw-rate RMSE; report every trajectory and IMO metric regardless.
predictions.stable_away_from_new_bound_rule: abs(q) <= 9.5 for a relaxed coefficient (at least 5% of the relaxed half-width away from either boundary).

task2.premise_correction: The immutable source fit has two exact bound hits, Y_R and X_vr, not three. N_rrr is interior. Only the two reproducible hits were relaxed.

premise_audit.discrepancy_disposition: No third coefficient is designated: the immutable source artifact has only two final values at a bound. N_rrr, the closest remaining normalized magnitude, is q=1.227368934 and is not a bound hit.

method.changed_only: Y_R and X_vr normalized bound half-width: 2 to 10

result.interpretation: Relaxing the reproducible active bounds did not meet the preregistered substantial-improvement rule; the too-tight-bound explanation is not supported by this check.
result.provenance_finding: The coefficient baseline values are recorded from Yasukawa & Yoshimura (2015) Table 3. The +/-2 optimization bounds are a repository identification choice, not literature-sourced physical bounds; therefore there is no evidence that the numeric bounds were copied from a different hull scale.
result.claim_limit: KVLCC2 model-scale Task 2 diagnostic only. This does not change the original Vehicle B protocol, fit, scoped negative result, or Vehicle-B-USV parameters.

task2.conclusion: Fivefold wider bounds produced stable interior solutions just beyond the old bounds, but all four held-out zig-zags worsened and the preregistered substantial-improvement criterion failed. Tight original bounds are not supported as the explanation.

task3.name: KVLCC2 full-scale structural check
task3.reason: Task 1 did not support the coverage-gap hypothesis; instructions require stopping for review rather than proceeding on the current assumption.

sign_or_frame.conclusion: No ingestion sign/frame error is indicated. Reflected signs agree and all six raw kinematic mapping checks pass, but strict mirror symmetry fails, especially for 20/20 zig-zags; timing and/or physical asymmetry remains.

transverse_propeller_rotation_force.evidence: propeller wrench is [axial thrust, 0, 0]; no rotation-direction parameter or transverse propeller force exists

asymmetry_representation.conclusion: The model can represent asymmetric rudder inflow through unequal gamma_R branches, but cannot represent propeller-walk force from screw rotation.

multistart.interpretation: This five-start test does not demonstrate the preregistered form of optimizer non-uniqueness; it does not prove identifiability.

overall_interpretation: The tested data-coverage and tight-bound explanations do not account for the transient failures. No simple ingestion sign/frame error is indicated. Real port/starboard asymmetry is present in the measurements and only partly representable by the model. The preregistered multi-start non-uniqueness rule was not met, although one higher-training-cost solution had much better held-out errors, pointing to possible objective mismatch rather than demonstrated equal-cost local minima. Model-form mismatch and identifiability limitations remain open.
claim_limit: Separate diagnostic campaign only. It does not relax, supersede, or reinterpret the original preregistered Vehicle B result, and it does not validate Vehicle B USV coefficients.
